summary.headline: 1000000211: 3 of 7 documented 99215 claims (43%) are documented below the billed level
summary.rationale: 1000000211 billed 99215 on 7.1% of 622 claims against an expected 3.9% given patient complexity (risk-adjusted score 1.60; plain z-score vs peers 0.13). 59% of this provider's 99215 claims were on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Records came back for 72 claims. Of 7 documented 99215 claims, 3 (43%) were documented below the billed level, against 42% for the comparison providers. Note checks on 59 returned notes (share showing each sign): problems 46%, late 3%, unsigned 0%, data 5%. No audit trail was received. 5 of 46 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed had no lab or test line on the claim. This pattern is consistent with upcoding. It is a reason to review the records, not a finding. Examples: C0091898: billed 99215, patient aged 56 with 0 chronic condition(s); documented MDM level moderate, 33 minutes. C0091903: billed 99215, patient aged 18 with 0 chronic condition(s); documented MDM level low, 29 minutes. C0091923: billed 99215, patient aged 32 with 0 chronic condition(s); documented MDM level moderate, 29 minutes. C0091759: billed 99215, patient aged 27 with 0 chronic condition(s). C0091788: billed 99215, patient aged 81 with 0 chronic condition(s). C0091858: billed 99215, patient aged 55 with 1 chronic condition(s) (hypertension); documented MDM level high, minutes not recorded.
next_steps: Request the full charts for C0091898, C0091903, C0091923 and have a certified coder re-score each against the current E/M rules (medical decision making or total time).
If the re-scoring confirms the pattern, review the random sample in the recovery packet's sampling plan before any overpayment estimate; do not extrapolate from a targeted sample.
Look at the notes themselves: 46% address fewer problems than their level implies and 3% were signed late; request the audit trail for C0091898, C0091903, C0091923.
